subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Find the equations of the tangents to 9x² + 16y² = 144, which make equal intercepts on the coordinate axes.

mark_split.label: Standard form and the equal-intercept line

insider_note: 'Equal intercepts on the axes' always means slope m = ±1 — writing the line as x ± y + k = 0 straight away, instead of x/p + y/p = 1, is the fast route to the tangent formula.

steps.label: Standard form and the equal-intercept line
steps.margin_note: First two marks. A line with equal intercepts always has slope ±1.
steps.memory_tip: 'Equal intercepts on the axes' is the signal for m = ±1 — no other information is needed to get the slope.
lines: A line making equal intercepts on the axes is x ± y + k = 0, so its slope is m = ±1
Equation of the tangent with slope m: y = mx ± √(a²m² + b²)
steps.why: A line x/p + y/p = 1 has equal intercepts p on both axes; rewriting it as x ± y = p shows its slope must be ±1, which is the only fact the tangent formula needs.
common_mistakes: Trying to introduce a separate intercept variable p instead of going straight to slope m = ±1.
Using a² = 9, b² = 16 by reading the equation's coefficients directly instead of dividing by 144 first.

steps.label: Final tangent equations
steps.margin_note: Last two marks. Both signs of m give tangents, so the ± on m combines with the ± from the formula.
steps.memory_tip: Equal-intercept tangents to an ellipse come in a symmetric family: y = ±x ± (same number).
steps.why: Substituting m = ±1 into the tangent formula gives the same constant √25 = 5 for both signs of m, so all four combinations of sign produce the four tangent lines with equal intercepts.
common_mistakes: Only writing the m = 1 case and dropping the m = −1 case, which loses half the answer.
